4045.body:
[CI] Fix native build failures on release/3.119.x (#4045)

Context: #4014, #4022, #3743, #4013

Four independent CI failures were blocking all builds on the 3.119.x
release branch. Each fix is backported from main and adapted to the
older file layout (scripts/ vs scripts/infra/).

~~ ANGLE WinAppSDK download (WinError 10013) ~~

DevDiv 1ES agents block Python's urllib from making outbound HTTPS
connections. Replace the winappsdk_setup.py invocation with a Cake
DownloadFile() from dnceng's dotnet-public feed, followed by a new
PowerShell script (generate_winappsdk_headers.ps1) that runs winmdidl
+ midlrt to produce the C++ headers ANGLE needs.

~~ WASM Emscripten 2.0.6 hang ~~

The 2.0.6 build intermittently hangs in CI. No .NET release ever
consumed this version — it was a legacy artifact from early
experimentation. Remove it from the matrix and merge lists.

~~ Tizen SDK 6.1 permanently broken ~~

Samsung rebranded Tizen Studio to Tizen SDK starting with version 10.0
and the old 6.1 Certificate-Manager package fails deterministically
with NoClassDefFoundError. Update to SDK 10.0 with the new URL pattern.

~~ Alpine apk.static transient download failures ~~

GitLab returns intermittent HTTP 5xx for apk.static. Without --fail,
curl silently saves the error body and the script tries to chmod +x a
JSON string. Add --fail --retry 5 --retry-delay 10 --retry-all-errors.

3716.title: [CI] Free disk space on hosted Linux agents (#3712)
3716.body:
[CI] Free disk space on hosted Linux agents (#3712)

Linux hosted agents (ubuntu-22.04/24.04) ship at ~93% disk usage,
leaving only ~5 GB free on a 72 GB disk. This caused Android emulator
test jobs to be abandoned when the agent ran out of space mid-build.

Add `scripts/free-disk-space-linux.sh`, a reusable cleanup script that
runs early in the bootstrapper for all hosted Linux builds. It removes
pre-installed toolchains and Android SDK components that SkiaSharp CI
never uses, freeing ~30 GB on current agent images:

  * Unused toolchains: .NET (4.6G, we install our own via UseDotNet@2),
    Swift (3.3G), Haskell (3.7G), Go (1.1G), CodeQL (1.7G), Julia (1G),
    Python (1.7G), Miniconda (858M), PyPy (524M), Ruby (312M),
    PowerShell modules (178M), Chromium, AWS CLI/SAM (515M)
  * Android SDK: NDK (6.5G, native builds use Docker or install their
    own), cmake, system-images, sources, extras, emulator (all
    explicitly reinstalled by the Android test job when needed)
  * Old build-tools versions (keeps only the latest)
  * Unused platform versions (keeps only those in ANDROID_PLATFORM_VERSIONS)

Components the script preserves because the bootstrapper skips Android
SDK installation on Linux (relies on the pre-installed SDK):
  * cmdline-tools — sdkmanager, used by install-android-package.ps1
  * platform-tools — adb, used for emulator communication
  * latest build-tools — aapt/d8 for .NET Android builds
  * required platforms — read from $ANDROID_PLATFORM_VERSIONS at runtime

The script is gated behind `pool.name == 'Azure Pipelines'` so it only
runs on Microsoft-hosted images and does not touch self-hosted agents.

3217.title: Add Linux Bionic native assets support
3217.body:
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/discussions/3205
Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/3206

Android uses the Bionic libc rather than glibc or musl, so the existing Linux
native asset packages did not cover that environment. This change adds a
dedicated `linux-bionic` runtime flavor for x64 and arm64, and wires it through
the SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp packaging so those binaries can be restored and
copied like the existing Linux variants.

The build keeps the current `externals-linux` flow and teaches it about the
Bionic-specific differences required by the Android NDK toolchain: disable
fontconfig, force the Unix debug path so `SkDebugf` is still provided, use the
NDK clang/llvm-ar tools explicitly, and create the small pthread stub needed
because the Linux GN configuration still links `-lpthread` even though Bionic
folds pthread support into libc.

This also adds the Docker-based local build environment and CI wiring needed to
produce the new assets reliably on both supported architectures. The Bionic jobs
are handled explicitly in the Linux pipeline so they do not inherit the generic
fontconfig expectations from the glibc builds, and the NoDependencies package
reuses the same Bionic binaries since that build already excludes the external
fontconfig dependency.

3076.title: [Android] Fix SKGLView not rendering after tab switch in MAUI TabBar
3076.body:
[Android] Fix SKGLView not rendering after tab switch in MAUI TabBar (#3076)

Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/2550
Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/2445

An `SKGLView` placed inside a MAUI `TabBar` renders correctly on first
display but goes blank when the user switches to another tab and back.
The same symptom occurs when navigating away from a page containing an
`SKGLView` and then returning.

The root cause is in `GLTextureView.OnAttachedToWindow()`. When the view
is reattached, a new `GLThread` is created with `width = 0` and
`height = 0`. The thread expects `OnLayoutChange()` to supply the real
dimensions, but Android does not fire that callback when the view is
reattached at the same size — the layout hasn't changed, so there is no
event. The GL surface is created at 0×0 and nothing is drawn.

Pass the current `Width` and `Height` of the `GLTextureView` into the
`GLThread` constructor so it starts with the correct dimensions
immediately. When the view appears for the first time, both values are
still 0, matching the previous default, so first-display behavior is
unchanged.

3633.title: Delay-load D3D12 DLLs to prevent crashes on systems without DX12
3633.body:
Some Windows systems do not have the full Direct3D stack available,
including d3d12.dll, dxgi.dll, or D3DCompiler_47.dll. Because
libSkiaSharp.dll linked against these DLLs as regular imports, the
native library could fail to load at process startup even for apps that
only use CPU rendering.

Update the Windows native build to mark the Direct3D dependencies as
delay-loaded and link with delayimp.lib so they are only resolved when
Direct3D is actually used. This preserves Direct3D support where it is
available, while allowing CPU-only scenarios to run on machines without
those components installed.

Also extend the Windows dependency verification step to distinguish
between regular imports and delay-loaded imports so CI can assert the
intended linker behavior.

Fixes #3267

3625.title: Reduce disk usage in Docker sample builds
3625.body:
The Linux Samples CI job consistently runs out of disk space (95%+ used)
because the samples-prepare task bulk-copies ALL platform nupkg files
(Android, iOS, Win32, etc.) into every Docker sample's packages/ directory
upfront. This wastes significant disk space on packages that will never be
used by the Docker build.

Changes:
- Move nupkg staging from samples-prepare into the per-sample Docker loop
  in samples-run, so only one set of packages exists on disk at a time
- Filter nupkg files by platform: on Linux skip Android/iOS/macOS/Win32
  native assets; on Windows skip Android/iOS/macOS/Linux native assets
- Delete staged nupkg files immediately after each Docker sample completes
- Remove Docker images (docker rmi) after each sample test to reclaim
  image layer space
- Run docker system prune after each Docker sample to clean up dangling
  layers from failed or completed builds

Together these changes should recover several GB of disk space during the
samples stage, preventing the 'no space left on device' errors seen in
builds 156518, 156522, and 156496.

3589.title: Refactor SKManagedStream: replace parent/child chain with SKData snapshot
3589.body:
Replace the fragile parent/child weak-reference ownership chain in
SKManagedStream with a lazy SKData snapshot approach for duplicate/fork.

OnDuplicate() now creates a native SkMemoryStream backed by a cached,
ref-counted SKData snapshot of the .NET stream. OnFork() duplicates and
seeks to the current position. The original stream remains fully readable
after duplication, multiple duplicates are allowed, and each duplicate is
an independent native stream with no managed interop overhead.

This is both simpler and faster than the old approach:
- No parent/child weak references or ownership transfer logic
- No VerifyOriginal() / InvalidOperationException on the original stream
- Snapshot is cached (one read, shared by all duplicates)
- Native SkMemoryStream duplicates expose getMemoryBase(), enabling
  zero-copy fast paths in Skia (e.g. CoreText font loading on macOS)

Tests updated to reflect new semantics:
- Removed SkipOnNonWindows() from 6 tests (no longer throws in native
  delegates, so all platforms can run these tests now)
- Added NonSeekableStreamDuplicateAndForkReturnNull test
- Renamed DotNetStreamIsClosedWhenSKManagedStreamIsDisposed to document
  that the .NET stream is closed when the parent is disposed (the
  snapshot keeps duplicates alive independently via native ref-counting)

Based on the original SKManagedStream refactoring from PR #3560.

3562.title: Fix Cairo assertion crash in GTK4 SKDrawingArea
3562.body:
Add pix.Flush() before pix.MarkDirty() to properly release any
existing Cairo snapshot references before modifying pixel data.

Without this call, Cairo's internal snapshot mechanism can trigger
an assertion failure (or corrupt rendering) because MarkDirty()
invalidates the surface while a snapshot still holds a reference
to the underlying data. The Flush() call tells Cairo to finish
any pending reads from prior snapshots, making it safe to then
mark the surface as modified.

This matches the documented Cairo usage pattern:
  cairo_surface_flush()   — complete pending reads
  <modify pixel data>     — write via Skia
  cairo_surface_mark_dirty() — notify Cairo of changes

The crash manifests as a SIGABRT or assertion on repeated redraws
when Cairo internally snapshots the ImageSurface (e.g. during
SetSourceSurface/Paint cycles).

3494.title: Fix Linux ARM64 crash: add fontconfig runtime library to cross-compile sysroot
3494.body:
## Summary

Fixes hard crash on Linux ARM64 with `undefined symbol: uuid_generate_random` by adding the fontconfig runtime library to all cross-compile Docker sysroots.

## Root Cause

The ARM64 cross-compile Docker only downloaded `libfontconfig1-dev` which provides:
- Headers and static library
- **Broken symlink**: `libfontconfig.so -> libfontconfig.so.1.12.0` (target doesn't exist!)

The actual shared library is in the **runtime package** (`libfontconfig1`). The linker silently skipped `-lfontconfig` when the symlink target was missing, resulting in:
- `libSkiaSharp.so` missing `libfontconfig.so.1` from DT_NEEDED
- Runtime crash when fontconfig (loaded via freetype) called `uuid_generate_random()`

## Changes

- **Dockerfiles 10, 11, 12, 13**: Download both `libfontconfig1-dev` AND `libfontconfig1`
- **native/linux/build.cake**: Add `--verifyIncluded` parameter (inverse of `verifyExcluded`)
- **CI YAML**: Add `--verifyIncluded=fontconfig` to verify fontconfig is linked in regular builds
- **Build scripts**: Pass through extra arguments to cake

## Testing

- ✅ Local: Built arm64, arm, x86, loongarch64 with verifyIncluded=fontconfig
- ✅ CI: All native Linux builds passed with fontconfig verification

Fixes #3369
Fixes #3272  
Fixes #3436

- Update releasing.md with CI feed documentation

* Remove package caching from feed management script

Since we now check if packages exist in the destination feed before
downloading, caching is unnecessary. Packages are now downloaded to
a temp directory, pushed immediately, and cleaned up.

This fixes disk space issues on CI runners where caching thousands
of large packages was filling up the runner.

* Remove state file tracking from feed management script

Since CI runs on fresh images, state file provides no value - packages
are already checked against destination feed before download. Removed:

- StateFile parameter
- Get-State and Save-State functions
- All state tracking (CopiedPackages, MovedPackages, DeletedVersions, etc.)
- State artifact uploads from workflow

The script is now fully stateless and idempotent.

* Allow PR script to find non-successful builds

The script now tries in order:
1. Successful completed builds
2. Any completed builds (failed tests but artifacts may be fine)
3. In-progress builds (artifacts may already be published)

This allows downloading artifacts even when tests are still running
or have failed, since the NuGet packages are typically ready earlier.

* Simplify PR script: remove Filter param, add SuccessfulOnly flag

- Remove -Filter parameter, always extract prerelease packages (*-*.nupkg)
- Always find the latest build by default (regardless of status)
- Add -SuccessfulOnly flag to restrict to successful builds only

- Same options: --successful-only, --force, --list, --build-id
- Updated docs with bash one-liner and options table

* Split _NativeAssets.* into separate parallel jobs

Each _NativeAssets.{platform} package now has its own job:
- _NativeAssets.alpine, alpinenodeps, android, ios, iossimulator
- _NativeAssets.linux, linuxnodeps, maccatalyst, nanoserver, osx
- _NativeAssets.tizen, tvos, uwp, wasm, watchos, windows, winui

This prevents disk space exhaustion from processing all platforms in one job.
